sample sample

Each example is organized around a capability domain of SDK and can be read and run independently. The example default connection is http://127.0.0.1:10026. If your service address is different, please modify the default configuration in the example first (Python: python/examples/common.py; most C++ examples support passing base_url on the command line; the only C# example is RuntimeBasic, whose address is configured with an environment variable).

After downloading and extracting atom_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center, each language’s examples are placed beside its package: python/examples/, cpp/examples/, and csharp/examples/.

Python Example

python/examples/:

Python examples accept environment variables such as ATOM_BASE_URL, ATOM_GRAPH_NAME, and ATOM_EPICRAW_FILE, so users can configure the service and input files without editing the source.

File Function

basic_usage.py

The most basic connectivity and main process examples, it is recommended to start from here

graph_examples.py

GraphService All public method examples

node_examples.py

NodeService All public method examples

graph_node_examples.py

GraphNodeService All public method examples

runtime_examples.py

RuntimeService All public method examples

Check the specific calling method according to the method name, and directly search for the example_方法名 function in the corresponding file; each example_ function is also supplemented with a brief description (what this method does, in what scenarios it is generally used, and which parameters need to be replaced with real values). Some examples use placeholder paths (such as /path/to/demo_graph.atom), which need to be replaced with the real file path of the local machine before running.

If you just want to get started quickly, look at basic_usage.py first.

C++ Example

cpp/examples/:

C++ examples accept the graph name, node IDs, and base_url as command-line arguments and do not depend on fixed internal node IDs.

File Function

basic_runtime.cpp

The most basic RuntimeService connectivity examples: list loaded graphs (list_graphs), load graphs (load_graph), view runtime metainformation (get_meta_info)

graph_workflow.cpp

GraphService The whole editing process: create the graph → open the graph → use NodeService to create nodes and set parameters → GraphService.run_graph to run the entire graph

graph_node_workflow.cpp

GraphNodeService The whole process is symmetrical with graph_workflow.cpp but the operation object is inside the subgraph node: open the subgraph → create nodes in the subgraph and set parameters → GraphNodeService.run_graph run the subgraph

runtime_workflow.cpp

RuntimeService The whole process of running state: load the graph → view meta information → set shared parameters/running parameters → construct RuntimeFrame and run_graph → read binding output (get_binded_outputs_info)

run_single_node.cpp

RuntimeService.run_single_node_json: Don’t rely on the entire graph, directly pass JSON input to a single node and run it

test_activation.cpp

calls NodeService.activate_node and GraphNodeService.activate_node multiple times in succession to verify whether the node activation/polling behavior is as expected

C# Example

There is currently only one RuntimeBasic project under csharp/examples/:

Configure the C# example with ATOM_BASE_URL, ATOM_GRAPH_NAME, ATOM_GRAPH_NODE_ID, ATOM_EPICRAW_FILE, and ATOM_IMAGE_FILE; real graph and input files are required before running it.

Directory Function

RuntimeBasic

Single file Program.cs goes through the typical call chain in sequence: first use GraphService.ListGraphSummariesAsync, NodeService.CreateNodeInfoAsync, GraphNodeService.OpenGraphInfoAsync to simply show the existence of the editing interface, and then the main line transfers to RuntimeService: ListGraphsAsync → LoadGraphAsync → GetMetaInfoModelAsync → SetSharedParamsAsync/SetRunParamsAsync → Structure RuntimeFrame and RunGraphAsync → GetBindedOutputsInfoAsync reads the output binding → RunSingleNodeNoGraphAsync/RunSingleNodeNoGraphJsonAsync demonstrates running a single node directly without building a graph → finally ReleaseGraphAsync releases the graph

C# SDK currently only has this sample project, covering fewer scenarios than Python/C++ (there is no separate graph/node/graph_node sample according to Service). This is the status quo, not a lack of documentation - when running from the SDK archive, csharp/examples/NuGet.Config uses the C# nupkg beside it. For more usage, please refer to Atom SDK — C# Version.
